messages.content: I forgot my Gmail password and can't sign in. How do I get back into my account?

You can get back in through Google's account recovery. It usually takes a few minutes.

1. Go to Google's **account recovery** page.
2. Enter the details it asks for, starting with your Gmail address.
3. Answer the questions as best you can. If you're not sure of an answer, make your best guess. A wrong guess doesn't lock you out, and you can try again.
4. When asked, create a **new password** that you haven't used for this account before.

**Stay safe while you do this:**
- Google staff can't help you sign in over the phone, so ignore anyone who calls or messages offering to recover your account.
- Never share your password or any verification code with anyone.

If it doesn't work right away, wait a few days and try again.

sources.title: Google Account Help: How to recover your Google Account or Gmail

messages.content: My granddaughter called crying and said she's in jail and needs bail money wired right now. It really sounded like her. Is this real?

Please **don't send any money yet**. Scammers can now copy a person's voice from a short recording, like a video posted online, so a call can sound exactly like someone you love.

Here's what to do:

1. **Hang up.** You don't need to argue or explain.
2. **Call your granddaughter** at the phone number you already have for her, not a number from the call.
3. If you can't reach her, **call another family member** or one of her friends to check.

**Warning signs of this scam:** an urgent emergency, pressure to act fast, and a request to **wire money, send cryptocurrency, or buy gift cards**. Those payments are very hard to get back.

If it turns out to be a scam, you can report it at **ReportFraud.ftc.gov**. If you already sent money, tell me right away and we'll work out the next steps.

sources.title: FTC Consumer Alert: Scammers use AI to enhance their family emergency schemes

messages.content: I got a text saying USPS couldn't deliver my package and I need to click a link to update my address. I am expecting a package. Should I click it?

Please **don't click the link**. Texts like this are a common scam, even when you really are expecting a package. The link usually leads to a fake website that looks real and asks for your personal or card information.

Instead:

1. **Don't click** the link or reply.
2. Check on your package using the website or app of the **store where you bought it**. Go there directly, not through the text.
3. **Report the text.** Use your phone's **junk** or **spam** reporting option if you see one, or forward the text to **7726**.
4. Then delete it.

If you already clicked and typed in your card number, call your bank right away using the number on the back of your card.

messages.content: I got an email from my pastor asking me to buy five $100 gift cards for church members and send him the numbers on the back. He said he's in a meeting and can't talk. Should I do it?

Please **don't buy the gift cards**. This is a common scam. Real businesses, government agencies, and people you know don't ask to be paid with gift card numbers, and once you share the numbers, the money is very hard to get back.

Here's what to do:

1. **Don't reply** to the email.
2. **Call your pastor** using a phone number you already have, or call the church office, and ask if he really sent it.
3. If it's fake, you can report it at **ReportFraud.ftc.gov**.

**If you already bought cards and shared the numbers:**
- Call the **gift card company** right away and ask for your money back. Sometimes they can freeze what's left on the card.
- Keep the cards and the store receipt.
- Report it at **ReportFraud.ftc.gov**.

messages.content: How do I set up Family Sharing on my iPhone so my daughter can be part of it?

Here's how to start a family group and invite your daughter. It takes a few minutes.

**Create the group:**
1. Open **Settings** and tap **your name** at the top.
2. Tap **Family**.
3. Follow the instructions on the screen to set up your family group.

**Invite your daughter:**
4. Go to **Settings**, then **Family**.
5. Tap the **add member** button (it has a plus sign).
6. Tap **Invite Others** and follow the steps to send her an invitation.

Once she accepts, she'll be part of your family group. If she doesn't see the invitation, go to **Settings**, then **Family**, tap her name, and choose **Resend Invitation**.

messages.content: Someone keeps calling me from the same number and hanging up. How do I block it on my iPhone?

You can block that number from your list of recent calls. It takes less than a minute.

1. Open the **Phone** app.
2. Tap **Recents**.
3. Find the number and tap it. (If you see a small **"i"** in a circle next to the number, tap that instead.)
4. Scroll down and tap **Block Caller**.
5. Confirm if asked.

After that, calls from that number won't ring your phone, and the caller won't be told they're blocked. If they leave a voicemail, it's saved, but you won't get a notification.

messages.content: I get a lot of spam calls from numbers I don't know. Can I make my iPhone only ring for people in my contacts?

iPhone can silence calls from numbers that aren't in your contacts and send them to voicemail. It takes about a minute.

1. Open the **Settings** app.
2. Tap **Apps**, then **Phone**.
3. Scroll to **Screen Unknown Callers** and tap it.
4. Choose **Silence**.

Calls from people in your contacts will still ring normally. Unknown callers go to voicemail, so check your voicemail now and then in case a doctor's office or pharmacy calls from a new number.

Tip: save important numbers, like your doctor and pharmacy, to your contacts so they always ring through.

messages.content: Can my Google Pixel phone filter out spam calls automatically?

The Phone app on your Pixel can filter spam calls. It takes about a minute to turn on.

1. Open the **Phone** app.
2. Tap the **More options** menu (three dots).
3. Tap **Settings**.
4. Tap **Caller ID and spam**.
5. Make sure **See caller ID & spam** is on.
6. Turn on **Filter spam calls**.

Filtered calls won't ring or notify you, but they still appear in your call history.

If you don't see **Filter spam calls**, your phone may use **Call Screen** instead, where spam blocking is one of the options. Tell me and I'll walk you through it.

messages.content: My iPhone battery seems to die quickly. How do I check the battery health?

You can check it in Settings. It takes a minute.

1. Open the **Settings** app.
2. Tap **Battery**.
3. Tap **Battery Health**. On some versions the name is slightly different.
4. Look at **Maximum Capacity**. This compares your battery now to when it was new. A lower number means it won't last as long between charges.

If you see a message that your battery's health is **significantly degraded**, it isn't a safety problem, but a new battery would help it last longer. Apple offers battery service, and it may be covered if your phone is still under warranty.

messages.content: How do I send one text message to my three kids at the same time on my iPhone?

You can start a group text. It takes about a minute.

1. Open the **Messages** app.
2. Tap the **Compose** button (a square with a pencil) at the top.
3. Type the name of your first child and choose them. Do the same for the other two. You can also tap the **plus** button to pick them from your contacts.
4. Type your message.
5. Tap the **Send** button (the up arrow).

All three will get the message, and when anyone replies, everyone in the group sees it.

If one of your kids has an Android phone and the message won't send, go to **Settings**, then **Messages**, and make sure **MMS Messaging** is turned on.

messages.content: Is there a way to make every website bigger in Chrome on my computer, so I don't have to zoom in each time?

You can change Chrome's default zoom so every website opens bigger. It takes about a minute.

1. Click the **More** menu (three dots) at the top right of Chrome.
2. Click **Settings**.
3. Click **Appearance**.
4. Find **Page zoom** and choose a bigger number, like **125%** or **150%**.

Every website will now open at that size.

To zoom in on just one page, hold the **Ctrl** key and press **+** (on a Mac, use the **Command** key instead).

messages.content: How can I share my location with my daughter on my iPhone so she knows I got home safe?

You can do this in the **Find My** app. It takes about two minutes. You and your daughter both need iPhones with a recent software update.

1. Open the **Find My** app.
2. Tap **Me** at the bottom, and make sure **Share My Location** is turned on.
3. Tap **People** at the bottom.
4. Tap the **Add** button (a plus sign), then tap **Share My Location**.
5. Choose your daughter.
6. Choose how long to share, such as **one hour**, **until the end of the day**, or **indefinitely**. Some versions also let you pick a custom time.

Your daughter can then see where you are in her Find My app.

Only share your location with people you trust.

sources.title: Apple Support: Share your location with iPhone

messages.content: How do I share my location with my son using Google Maps on my Android phone?

Here's how. It takes about two minutes. Your son needs a Gmail address, saved in your contacts.

1. Open **Google Maps** and make sure you're signed in.
2. Tap your **profile picture or initial** at the top.
3. Tap **Location sharing**.
4. Tap **New share**.
5. Choose how long to share your location.
6. Choose your son. If Maps asks to see your contacts, allow it.
7. Tap **Share**.

Your son can then see where you are in Google Maps.

If he doesn't use Gmail, you can share a **link** instead, which works for up to 24 hours. Only share your location with people you trust.

sources.title: Google Maps Help: Share your real-time location with others (Android)

messages.content: How do I download the WhatsApp app on my iPhone?

You can get it from the **App Store**. It takes a couple of minutes.

1. Open the **App Store** app.
2. Tap **Search** at the bottom.
3. Type **WhatsApp** and tap the search button.
4. Find the right app and tap **Get** next to it.
5. To confirm, double-click the **side button**. If your iPhone has Face ID, look at the screen. If it has Touch ID, rest your finger on the Home button. You may also be asked for your Apple Account password.

When the download finishes, the button changes to **Open** and the app appears on your Home Screen.

Tip: check the app's name and maker before tapping **Get**, so you get the real app and not a lookalike.

sources.title: Apple Support: Download apps on your iPhone or iPad
